title: Monstera

description.main: Shirana Shahbazi’s artist’s book Monstera (JRP|Ringier with Kunsthalle Bern, 2014) collects her studio abstractions: coloured geometric solids arranged as still lifes and photographed from shifting positions, 256 colour plates in a softcover edited with Manuel Krebs. Published alongside her Kunsthalle Bern exhibition of the same name, 25 October to 7 December 2014.
description.extended:
Shirana Shahbazi’s artist’s book Monstera gathers the abstract photographs she made in her Zurich studio around 2014, published by JRP|Ringier in collaboration with Kunsthalle Bern.

Edited by the artist with Manuel Krebs of the Zurich design studio NORM, the softcover runs to 256 pages and 256 colour plates. Shahbazi builds the pictures as still lifes rather than on a screen. She arranges coloured geometric solids in the studio and photographs them from shifting positions, with double exposures and overlaps that leave the eye unsure whether it is looking at a flat pattern or a group of objects. The cover layers the silhouette of a Monstera leaf over a photograph of a city at night. The book appeared alongside her exhibition of the same name at Kunsthalle Bern (25 October to 7 December 2014), curated by Fabrice Stroun and Tenzing Barshee.

Shahbazi was born in Tehran in 1974, moved to Germany as a child, and trained in Dortmund and Zurich, where she lives. Her earlier books include Goftare Nik / Good Words (Hatje Cantz, 2001), Meanwhile (JRP|Ringier, 2007) and Then Again (Steidl, with Fotomuseum Winterthur). She received the Prix Meret Oppenheim in 2019.
description.artist_bio: Shirana Shahbazi (b. 1974, Tehran) moved to Germany in 1985, studied photography and design in Dortmund (1995-97) and photography at Zurich University of the Arts (1997-2000), and lives in Zurich. Represented by Galerie Peter Kilchmann. Prizes: Citibank Private Bank Photography Prize (2002), Prix Meret Oppenheim (2019). Books: Goftare Nik / Good Words (Hatje Cantz, 2001), Meanwhile (JRP|Ringier, 2007), Then Again (Steidl), Monstera (JRP|Ringier, 2014), first things first (Sternberg Press, 2017).
description.exhibition_context: Monstera, Kunsthalle Bern, 25 October to 7 December 2014, curated by Fabrice Stroun and Tenzing Barshee. Upstairs: enlarged holiday snapshots from a 2014 family stay in Tehran, reprinted as two-colour lithographs on painted walls; lower level: the Monstera series of photographs of the houseplant's leaves.

notes: Shelf: Mixed. Artist's book published in collaboration with Kunsthalle Bern for the exhibition Monstera (25 October to 7 December 2014); edited by Manuel Krebs and Shirana Shahbazi. Publisher lists September 2014; D.A.P. US release February 2015.
